Azure (signed-in identity)

note: Application permissions are Microsoft Graph app roles granted (with admin consent) to the service principal EARM signs in with (AZURE_CLIENT_ID, or the managed identity). Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy replaces Application.ReadWrite.All for applications the service principal owns.
note: 2 resource(s) have a name that depends on another resource (for example a service principal named after reference(...).appId); their permissions are computed from the declaration and the references it contains.
note: Learn (application-post-owners, serviceprincipal-post-owners): adding an owner needs Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy AND Directory.Read.All, and "Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy isn't sufficient to add another owner": when the declared owners include anyone besides the principal that owns the application, grant Application.ReadWrite.All as well.
note: `ownerOf` on a user reads GET /users/{id}/ownedObjects, which Microsoft Graph does not support with application permissions (Learn: user-list-ownedobjects, Application: Not supported); the owner set of a user principal can only be reconciled with a signed-in (delegated) token. Declare `owners` on the application, service principal or group instead.
note: `manager` is written with PUT /users/{id}/manager/$ref (User.ReadWrite.All) but read with GET /users/{id}/manager, for which Learn lists no application permission (user-list-manager, Application: Not supported); with an application token that read can be refused (403), so reconcile `manager` with a signed-in (delegated) token.
note: Restoring soft-deleted objects (--on-soft-deleted-conflict restore): users need User.DeleteRestore.All, groups Group.ReadWrite.All, administrative units AdministrativeUnit.ReadWrite.All, applications and service principals Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy (Learn: directory-deleteditems-restore). Probing /directory/deletedItems before a create needs the type's read permission (for applications Application.Read.All, which Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy does not carry: the probe is then skipped with a SoftDeleteProbeSkipped warning).
note: Edge permissions are listed for every relationship property the template declares (including an empty array, which removes edges). Key Vault access is an Azure RBAC / access-policy requirement of the signed-in identity, not a Graph permission.
